identity.title: A D/H ratio consistent with Earth's water in Halley-type comet 12P from ALMA HDO mapping

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we present interferometric maps of water (H$_2$O) and semiheavy water (HDO) in the gas-phase coma of a comet (Halley-type comet 12P/Pons-Brooks), obtained using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

redshift_or_distance.value: perihelion r_H=0.78 au on 2024 April 21; phase angle ~30 deg

evidence.quote: 12P/Pons-Brooks is a Halley-type comet on a highly elliptical 71-year orbit, last reaching perihelion at $r_H=0.78$ au on 2024 April 21.

question.value: What is the D/H ratio in water of Halley-type comet 12P/Pons-Brooks, and is it consistent with Earth's ocean water and the origin of H2O in the coma?

evidence.quote: imply a coma D/H ratio (for water) of $(1.71\pm0.44)\times10^{-4}$
ALMA observations of H$_2$O, HDO and CH$_3$OH in comet 12P/Pons-Brooks were performed as part of program 2023.1.01143.L (PI: M. Cordiner)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit CH3OH for coma temperature, velocity and Q(H2O) proxy

method.value: SUBLIME 3D non-LTE model fitted to visibilities with two-region (hemispherically asymmetric) coma, segmented T(r), accelerated velocity law

evidence.quote: we first performed independent fits to the two CH$_3$OH datasets (April 18–25 and May 4), using models with variable $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $T_1(r)$, $T_2(r)$, $v_1$, $v_2$, $\phi$ and $\theta_{jet}$.

key_parameters.value: 4 T(r) segments for Apr 18–25; 3 for May 4

evidence.quote: we found that four segments were required in the $T(r)$ profile to obtain a good fit to the observations, whereas on May 4, only 3 segments were required

assumptions.value: Steady-state coma; electron density scaling x_ne=0.2; collisional cross-section with H2O 5e-14 cm^-2; T1=T2

evidence.quote: with an electron density scaling factor of $x_{ne}=0.2$

fitting.value: chi^2 minimization with lmfit, Levenberg-Marquardt, across all baselines and spectral channels

evidence.quote: the $\chi^2$ statistic was minimized across all baselines and spectral channels with the `lmfit` Python code (cite: new16), using the Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least-squares algorithm

validation.value: Reduced chi-square near 1; abundance within 5% across velocity-law choices

evidence.quote: all three models had best-fitting abundances within 5% of each other

analysis_steps.goal: Retrieve H2O production rate on May 4

method.value: Iterate H2O and CH3OH retrievals until T(r) and Q(H2O) converge; fit p-H2O with theta_jet=90, phi=phi_STO, psi=PSAng fixed; v1, v2, Q1, Q2 free; OPR=3

evidence.quote: we iteratively improved $T(r)$ and $Q({\rm H_2O})$ by running successive retrievals on CH$_3$OH and H$_2$O, feeding the results of one retrieval into the other, until the respective model parameters converged.
The p-H$_2$O/H$_2$O mixing ratio was fixed at 0.25 (see Methods).

claims.hypothesis: Is the D/H in water of HTC 12P consistent with Earth's oceans?
claims.experiment: Fit SUBLIME model to ALMA HDO and H2O visibilities, with CH3OH as proxy for Q(H2O)
claims.finding: Consistent with terrestrial ocean water, at the lower end of comet values

evidence.quote: This is consistent with the terrestrial (VSMOW) value of $1.56\times10^{-4}$, within the uncertainties.

claims.hypothesis: Do H2O and HDO come directly from the nucleus?
claims.experiment: Chi^2 analysis of production scale length
claims.result: L_p=0 preferred; upper limits 135 km (H2O), 610 km (HDO)

evidence.quote: For H$_2$O and HDO, the 99% confidence upper limits on their respective $L_p$ values are 135 km and 610 km

claims.hypothesis: Do comet dynamical families differ in D/H?
claims.finding: Differences cannot be established with current statistics

evidence.quote: although differences between these cometary families cannot be ruled out based on the (presently limited) statistics

why_this_data.value: 12P is among the brightest and most active periodic comets, an excellent target for remote spectroscopy

evidence.quote: 12P is among the brightest and most active known periodic comets, and thus presented an excellent opportunity for remote (ground-based) spectroscopy during its 2024 apparition.

why_this_method.value: Fourier-domain fitting avoids imaging artifacts from gridding and deconvolution

evidence.quote: The Fourier domain is used since it is native to the ALMA data, and therefore intrinsically avoids the imaging artifacts

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Distributed (icy grain) H2O source tested; no improvement in fit for parent-only model

evidence.quote: the quality of the fits (as monitored using the $\chi^2$ statistic) did not significantly improve through addition of distributed (coma) sources
